meaning: Number of descendants of Adonikam according to Nehemiah 7:18
description: The number 667 appears in Nehemiah 7:18 as the count of descendants of Adonikam who returned from exile in Babylon. Although the number carries no independent symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition, it is notable that the parallel list in Ezra 2:13 gives 666 for the same family. This difference of one number has attracted interest among textual critics and Bible interpreters but most likely stems from variations in manuscript traditions. Beyond this specific occurrence, 667 has no established symbolic role in the Bible, Talmud, or Jewish numerology.

versions.meaning: The number 667 has no known or established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: Unlike nearby numbers such as 666 (the number of the beast in Revelation), 667 holds no special symbolic role in the Bible, Talmud, or Jewish numerology (gematria). There are no known scriptures or rabbinic texts that attribute any particular spiritual or prophetic significance to this number. At best, it can be regarded as an ordinary number without religious symbolism in these traditions.
versions.reason: [major] The number 667 actually appears in the Bible – in Nehemiah 7:18 as the count of descendants of Adonikam. This is a concrete biblical occurrence that should be mentioned in the description. The claim that the number has no known role is therefore inaccurate.; [minor] The name Adonikam (אֲדֹנִיקָם) has an interesting meaning ('my lord has risen up') which could be explained in a footnote, especially since it is the only known biblical occurrence of the number 667.; [minor] It is worth noting the difference between Ezra 2:13 (which gives 666 for Adonikam's descendants) and Nehemiah 7:18 (which gives 667), as this textual-critical point is relevant and interesting.

footnotes.text: The name Adonikam (אֲדֹנִיקָם) means "my lord has risen" or "my lord rose," a theophoric name expressing trust in God's power.

The difference between 666 in Ezra 2:13 and 667 in Nehemiah 7:18 is one of several numerical discrepancies between the two lists of returnees. Such variations may be due to copying errors, different times of counting, or the fact that the two lists are based on different administrative sources.

The fact that Adonikam's descendants are counted as 666 in Ezra has led to speculation in some Christian interpretive traditions because of its connection to "the number of the beast" in Revelation 13:18, but this is an anachronistic reading without support in the original context.
